messages:
yasmin: Quick follow-up from the architecture sync. I sketched an "auto-tune safety case" for precision profiles so we can safely nudge customers toward lower-bit paths without surprise regressions. Need design review.
eli: short summary of the safety case?
yasmin: TL;DR: automatic tuning should (1) be conservative by default, (2) attach explainable evidence to every decision, and (3) provide an automatic rollback if empirical quality drifts beyond the customer's tolerance.
rob: ok. what's the control loop look like?
yasmin: three stages: collect (shadow-sample + fingerprint buckets), estimate (catalog priors + Bayesian update -> recommended profile + confidence), and enforce (runtime admission + hedged requests + ledger entries). If drift detected, auto-revert and surface a root-cause packet to the tenant.
eli: hedged requests = send a small percent to baseline bitpath for comparison, right? how small?
yasmin: default 2% hedged for low-uncertainty profiles, 5-10% when uncertainty is medium/high. hedged responses are traced and compared via anchors.
rob: comparison methodology? we can't run full eval for every hedged request.
yasmin: use sampled anchors and lightweight metrics: degscore, avg_confidence, and a categorical anchor-check every N hedged requests. aggregate using bootstrap to compute confidence intervals.
qa-bot: Reminder: make sure degscore and avg_confidence metrics are in runtime sampling whitelist.
eli: what about latency variability? lowbit can sometimes reduce token compute but increase p99 due to kernel fallbacks. We need safety checks for latency as well as quality.
yasmin: agreed. safety case includes dual thresholds: quality threshold (max_quality_loss_pct) and latency guard (p99_latency_delta_ms). If safety checks fail, runtime will switch new requests back to baseline immediately and mark the profile as "paused".
rob: how is "immediately" implemented without thrashing? race between many endpoints toggling?
yasmin: two mechanisms: (A) runway cooldown: after a revert, profile enters cooldown window (default 30m) where changes are rate-limited; (B) global circuit-backer for heavy churn that groups toggles and enforces exponential backoff per endpoint.
eli: customers will want control. UX surface?
yasmin: console shows recommended profile + uncertainty band, a toggle to enable auto-tune, hedging percent slider, and explicit rollback thresholds. Also provide an audit log entry and per-request ledger links for every decision.
rob: billing: how do we attribute cost savings for hedged requests? hedged requests increase tokens but are for safety. finance will need a net-savings calc that subtracts hedging overhead.
yasmin: ledger rows will include `token_savings_est` and `hedge_overhead_tokens`. billing panel shows net estimated monthly savings and hedging cost line item.
eli: edge case: multi-tenant endpoints where some callers want aggressive lowbit and others strict. plan for per-caller overrides?
yasmin: yes. profile at endpoint-level with per-caller JWT-scoped override. Overrides must be audited (override_actor) and obey org-wide caps (e.g., disallow lowbit for compliance orgs). ledger records override contexts.
qa-bot: Security note: do not store raw prompts in ledger. store hashed fingerprint + trace id only. Make redaction flow available.
rob: what about model changes? kernel upgrades or new quantized builds could change deltas. we need a revalidation trigger when model binary/revision changes.
yasmin: profile metadata includes `model_revision` and `catalog_curve_version`. On model change, profile moves to "stale" state and auto-schedules a quick re-sample before any further auto-tunes.
eli: nice. implementational asks: (1) decision payload must be compact for headers, (2) full evidence JSON goes to trace store, (3) ledger row stores summary for audit. Example header: `x-precision-decision: int8;reason=auto-tune;pred=0.7;conf=med;hedge=2%`
yasmin: exactly. runtime will emit header + trace.tag.precision.* fields and ledger row.
rob: rollout plan? small internal pilot first?
yasmin: pilot plan: (1) internal pilot on two non-critical endpoints @10% traffic with hedging=5% for 2 weeks, (2) invite 3 beta customers with explicit consent, (3) GA only after zero-sev regressions and mean savings verified.
ops-bot: Note: please link infra PR that adds `profile_state` and ledger columns. PR #1234.
eli: final Q: automated tuning frequency? how often do we re-evaluate?
yasmin: re-eval cadence default = daily for active profiles, but limited to once-per-cooldown-window. customers can request manual re-sample via console.
rob: sounds pragmatic. I want the safety-case appendix included in the RFC update. I'll review once posted.
yasmin: will post RFC appendix by EOD and attach pilot checklist. thanks for the input. :thumbsup:
